gml:Dictionary.gml:description: Codes naming the analytical approach a rigid inclusion design was calculated by. Used for the value of the designMethod property of diggs:RIProgramBasis. RI_Design_Parameter_Analysis.md Group A row 3 names four approaches in current practice; the list is open, since design methods are not a closed set.
gml:Dictionary.gml:name: DIGGS Rigid Inclusion Design Method Codelist Definitions

diggs:Definition.gml:description: An axisymmetric or plane-strain analysis of a single inclusion and its tributary soil area, treated as a repeating unit cell.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Unit-cell method

diggs:Definition.gml:description: An analysis based on a limit-equilibrium or empirical arching model - Marston, Hewlett-Randolph, Zaeske, adapted-Terzaghi, Prandtl or similar - that partitions embankment load between the inclusion heads and the soil between them.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Arching (load-transfer) method

diggs:Definition.gml:description: A numerical (finite element or finite difference) analysis modelling the inclusions, platform and supported structure explicitly rather than through a closed-form or limit-equilibrium formulation.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Finite element method

diggs:Definition.gml:description: An analysis enforcing compatible displacement between the inclusions and the soil between them, typically via t-z/q-z or similar load-transfer curves, rather than a fixed arching ratio.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Load-displacement-compatibility method

diggs:Definition.gml:description: The FHWA GEC-13 beam formulation (Eq 3-26), in which the load transfer platform is analysed as a beam or slab spanning between inclusion heads and the geosynthetic membrane contribution is taken through the membrane factor of GEC-13 Table 6-2. One of two FHWA variants a designer selects between; the other is fhwa_strain_compatibility.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: FHWA beam method

diggs:Definition.gml:description: The FHWA GEC-13 generalized parabolic formulation (Eq 3-25), which distributes load between the inclusion heads and the intervening soil by enforcing strain compatibility across the platform rather than assuming a fixed arching ratio. One of two FHWA variants a designer selects between; the other is fhwa_beam.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: FHWA strain-compatibility method

diggs:Definition.gml:description: The Nordic (Scandinavian) design practice for column-supported embankments, carried as a distinct published method in practitioner surveys of rigid inclusion design.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Nordic method
